extracted.intended_audience: State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), State governments, State Apprenticeship Councils, program sponsors, and apprenticeship stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory criteria and procedural requirements for recognition of State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), the advisory role and composition of State Apprenticeship Councils, SAA duties and limits on delegation, reciprocity processes, and the content/timing of State Apprenticeship Plans for Federal recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive non-delegable SAA authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A recognized SAA 'possesses the exclusive, non-delegable authority to evaluate, approve, register, monitor, oversee, suspend, and deregister apprenticeship programs operating within that State.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exclusivity is a precondition of recognition; the only exception is when the Administrator chooses to exercise residual authority to register a program on a State-by-State or nationwide basis (per existing 29 CFR 29.13(i)). The proposed §29.26(a) consolidates these SAA authorities into one location to reduce confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on delegating SAA functions to third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.26(b) would 'expressly prohibit a State—either in law or in practice—from delegating, assigning, or relinquishing any of the discretionary authority conferred by the Department upon an SAA ... to any external third-party entity, including a State Apprenticeship Council.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department cites complaints where authority was impermissibly ceded to councils or external entities, causing delays, lack of due process, and barriers to registration. States may still use contractors for functions that do not involve SAA duties, but the SAA must retain ultimate decision-making authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Apprenticeship Councils limited to advisory role
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.26(c) would 'limit the duties and powers of State Apprenticeship Councils to providing their respective SAAs with written, non-binding advice, recommendations, research, and reports concerning apprenticeship-related matters.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule removes any regulatory/advisory distinction and explicitly prohibits Councils from assuming discretionary or inherently governmental regulatory and oversight duties. Councils are expected to provide sector-balanced consensus advice; if Councils perform SAA-only functions the Administrator may initiate derecognition proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single State Apprenticeship Council per State
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule 'envisions the creation of a single State Apprenticeship Council' established by each SAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: multiple councils in one State could produce conflicting recommendations and reduce clarity for the SAA. Limiting to one Council helps convene stakeholders and produce consistent, consensus advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition requirements for State Apprenticeship Councils
rubrics_metrics.description: Councils must contain equal representation from employers (or employer organizations), labor organizations (including joint labor-management organizations), and members of the public; public members must not outnumber other sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.26(c)(1) adds granularity: employer and labor representatives may include individuals from sectors where apprenticeship is not widespread; public members must include at least one representative from the State workforce development system and at least one from secondary or postsecondary education familiar with registered apprenticeship. Councils are encouraged to reflect and include underserved communities and industry diversity to support expansion goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core SAA duties and responsibilities (consolidated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.26(a) enumerates SAA responsibilities, including establishing and implementing apprenticeship-related regulations, policies, and procedures to meet parts 29 and 30; day-to-day establishment, operation, oversight, monitoring of registered apprenticeship programs; promoting cohesion and alignment among program sponsors and employers; and serving as Registration Agencies for CTE apprenticeship under subpart B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These activities listed in (a) are those OA would perform if a State did not have a recognized SAA. Consolidation into one provision is intended to make expectations clear and reduce confusion about SAA responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-sharing requirement as condition of recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.26(a)(5) would require SAAs, as a precondition for initial or continued recognition, to provide OA with data relating to apprentices and registered apprenticeship programs in that State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department views this regulatory data-sharing requirement (and related §29.28) as enhancing transparency and providing a national picture of the National Apprenticeship System's performance; State Apprenticeship Plans are expected to operationalize data collection and reporting strategies, including disaggregated demographic outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAA retention of ultimate decision-making when using contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: SAAs may use contractors or third parties to perform tasks 'that do not involve or relate to duties described in proposed §29.26(a),' such as promotional and outreach activities, but 'the SAA must retain the ultimate decision-making authority regarding whether an apprenticeship program qualifies for registration.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting is permitted for non-core functions only; any functions that relate to registration determinations or oversight are non-delegable and must be retained by the SAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity process requirements and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.26(d) requires SAAs to establish a reciprocity process with a determination on a program sponsor's application for reciprocity no later than 45 calendar days after receipt. Proposed §29.26(d)(1)-(3) specify conditions under which reciprocal approval may be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocity may only be provided where: (1) the sponsor meets the statutory and regulatory wage and hour requirements and apprentice-to-journeyworker ratios of the State where reciprocity is sought; (2) the program and apprentices are registered by the originating Registration Agency; and (3) the SAA accounts for State or local licensure requirements by ensuring standards meet or exceed licensure requirements if licensure is required. The change responds to the need to balance access to registration status with State licensure and labor-law concerns; SAAs must articulate this process in their State Apprenticeship Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Apprenticeship Plan content and 4-year cycle for recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.27 establishes a State Apprenticeship Plan process as the framework for OA to confer recognition; Plans are due every 4 years and must include strategic planning elements to establish a vision for expansion, modernization, diversification, and equitable opportunities for learners and workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Plan is a blueprint for prioritizing Federal/State investments, aligning administrative/operational/governance principles, leveraging workforce and education infrastructure, promoting program quality and good jobs, galvanizing commitments for underserved communities, and specifying data collection/reporting strategies. The Department intends to make Plan contents publicly available to promote transparency and expects Plans to align with WIOA/Perkins planning cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: State law standard for recognition — meet or exceed Federal minimums
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.27 would modify the existing conformity standard by requiring that a State's apprenticeship laws 'either meet or exceed the minimum requirements set forth in 29 CFR parts 29 and 30 for protecting the safety and welfare of apprentices,' rather than strict conformity to federal regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: the prior conformity requirement impeded efficient consideration of recognition applications. The revised standard ensures SAAs satisfy minimum Federal labor and EEO requirements while allowing States flexibility to innovate and provide greater protections. This harmonizes with proposed 'Relation to Other Laws' provisions and supports regulatory flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator remedial authority and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The preamble explains that where State Apprenticeship Councils perform SAA-only functions, 'the Administrator can take appropriate remedial action including the initiation of derecognition proceedings,' and the Administrator retains residual authority to register programs under certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This serves as an enforcement backstop to ensure accountability and that oversight and regulatory functions remain with state government agencies (SAAs) accountable to the public. The Department cites complaints and past instances where it considered exercising plenary authority under existing §29.13(i).
